note: Style cards written for OpenMotion. Colour values and typeface choices are starting points; a supplied Brandkit wins. Fonts are open-licensed (SIL OFL, Apache-2.0 or GUST).

styles.name: Bauhaus
styles.idea: Circle, square, triangle and three primaries: beauty as a rule you can teach.
rules: Compose with two to four primitives: circle, square, triangle and their halves.
Flat red, yellow and blue on paper with black; one primary leads each scene.
Headlines in a bold geometric sans, set lowercase.
Balance big against small off-centre; empty paper is a shape too.
Snap edges to a grid and show structure with thick black bars.
motion: Shapes slide in along one axis and lock to grid lines on the beat.
A circle rolls, a square drops flat, a triangle tips over its corner.
Colour fields wipe across with a hard straight edge, never a fade.

styles.name: Swiss Style
styles.idea: One grid, one sans serif, one red: layout as a problem you can calculate.
rules: Lay down a 12-column modular grid before anything else; every edge sits on it.
One sans-serif family; hierarchy only through size and weight.
Flush left, ragged right.
One headline or one red block leads; balance it with generous white space.
Facts first: no decoration inside the information hierarchy.
motion: Grid lines draw first, then type snaps into the cells.
Large numerals slide by whole columns.
Cuts are hard; the only colour change is the red block arriving.

styles.name: Constructivism
styles.idea: Turn the axis 30 degrees and the page starts charging forward.
rules: Work on a main axis at -30 degrees with a perpendicular secondary axis; captions stay horizontal.
Red and black on warm paper; red is reserved for the main action.
Assemble wedges, circles and heavy bars as connected machine parts with sharp corners.
Crop a photo to one telling detail and lock it into the geometry.
Scale the key word until it breaks the frame; use real letters, never fake Cyrillic.
motion: Elements fire along the diagonal and stamp in on the beat with a 2-frame overshoot.
A red wedge pierces a black circle as the hero beat.
Scene changes are diagonal slashes along the secondary axis.

styles.name: Memphis
styles.idea: One colour per block, a black outline, a little tilt: ordinary things made fun.
rules: Build from circles, triangles, half circles and squiggles.
One flat candy colour per block; neighbours clearly different.
Black patterns (dots, squiggles, confetti) on large areas only; text sits on a quiet ground.
Tilt decorative pieces by 6, 12 or 18 degrees; dates, prices and body text stay level.
Outline everything in black with a hard offset shadow and zero blur.
motion: Blocks drop, squash about 24% on landing and spring back from their base.
Squiggles draw on like a tube being squeezed.
Background colour hands over with a wavy-edged sweep.

styles.name: Pop Art
styles.idea: Dots instead of gradients, thick ink around every colour: everyday objects on the gallery wall.
rules: Tone comes from dot size on a fixed spacing, never a blurred gradient.
Every colour area is enclosed by one consistent bold ink line with a hard offset shadow.
Flat red, yellow and blue with black and white; pink or cyan only as accents.
Repeat one image in a grid and recolour each copy instead of redrawing it.
Short loud words go in bursts; readable details go in calm speech or caption boxes.
motion: A grid of the same product recolours cell by cell on the beat.
Sound words punch in at 150% and settle with overshoot.
Halftone dots grow to fill the frame as the transition.

styles.name: Risograph
styles.idea: Two to four spot inks on breathing paper; the slight misregistration is the machine's accent.
rules: Choose two to four inks first; fluorescent pink is the signature.
Overlap inks with multiply so the overlap becomes a third colour.
Offset each ink layer by a few pixels; the miss is intentional.
Tint with dots or grain, never with opacity.
Keep a paper grain over everything.
motion: Each ink layer slides in separately, then snaps into near-registration.
One new sheet per beat, like pages coming off the drum.
Grain is re-seeded every 2–3 frames so the paper breathes.

styles.name: Neo-Brutalism
styles.idea: Black borders everywhere and a shadow that is a solid black offset: pressing means sliding onto the shadow.
rules: 3–4 px solid black border on every card, button, input, image and tag; one radius only.
Hard shadow with zero blur: 4 px for buttons, 8 px for cards; longer shadow means higher in the hierarchy.
Flat fills, no gradients; at most three fills per screen and the brightest goes to the key block.
Show the structure: dot-grid ground, visible dividers, monospaced numbers, 8 px spacing.
Tilt exactly one sticker or badge by 2–6 degrees.
motion: Buttons press by moving onto their shadow (shadow goes to 0) on the beat.
Cards slam in and land with a 1-frame squash.
Every slam and press lands on a beat or half-beat.

styles.name: Art Deco
styles.idea: Draw a central axis first; steps, sunbursts and triple lines grow out of it in mirrored pairs; gold is only for lines.

palette.name: gold
palette.role: thin lines, large titles, the one pressed block

rules: Draw one vertical axis and mirror layout, ornaments and buttons around it in pairs.
Masses step narrower as they rise; corners are cut in two steps, never rounded.
Hide the light behind the subject and radiate 18–24 thin rays over 180 degrees.
One line becomes three: one thick, two thin, gap about three times the thick line.
Gold only for lines, big titles and a single solid block; large areas stay onyx or emerald.
motion: One continuous camera that only pushes, rises or pulls back, never shakes.
Light runs along the triple lines from the axis outward.
Towers and ornaments rise in mirrored pairs, centre first.

styles.name: Liquid Glass
styles.idea: Glass does not glow; it bends what is behind it, and only at the edge.
rules: Bend, don't blur: displace only in the bevel ring and magnify the centre 3–6%; the background stays sharp.
Thickness is hierarchy: rows thin, buttons medium, sheets and players thickest.
Glass is for controls floating over content only; never glass on glass, never content cards of glass.
Pieces closer than about 24 px merge with a neck; a button growing into a menu is one continuous shape.
Pick text colour from the luminance behind the glass and keep 4.5:1 contrast.
motion: Controls morph continuously (button to menu, bar shrinking on scroll).
Two drops merge through a neck and split again.
Labels flip between black and white as darker content passes under them.
avoid: frosted blur plus white border (that is 2020 glassmorphism)

styles.name: Mid-Century Modern
styles.idea: Scissors instead of rulers: every piece is a cut paper sheet you could pick up, and its shadow is its height.
rules: Edges wobble by 1–1.6 px like scissor cuts; corners stay sharp; each piece tilts within ±3 degrees.
Shadow equals height: a sheet lifted h px casts an offset of (0.5h, h) with blur about 0.4h.
Where two inks overlap, multiply them, light over dark only.
Use atomic-age shapes: kidney, boomerang, starburst, orbit, ball-and-stick.
Warm paper plus candy colours in small doses; ink only for type.
motion: Paper sheets are lifted (shadow grows), moved and set down (shadow shrinks).
The same set of sheets flips over to become the next scene.
Pressed elements drop to zero height.

styles.name: Diorama
styles.idea: Cut the world into a base, build it piece by piece, then tilt-shift it small.

palette.name: soil
palette.role: cut base layers, dark to light

rules: Everything is a block that slams down: fall, squash about 16%, rebound from its base.
Show a square-cut base with layered soil; rooms lose two walls.
Long lens from about 30 degrees above, a sharp band over the subject, blur above and below.
In UI, the model is the control: tapping a piece toggles it.
Dusk light and windows lighting one by one make it feel lived in.
motion: Tiles land one after another 20–30 ms apart.
The camera glides on a smooth spline and never stops abruptly.
Windows light up in sequence as the finale.
avoid: cold blue night with white lights

styles.name: Low Poly
styles.idea: One face, one colour: turn the light and whole faces jump between three shades.
rules: Each triangle is one flat colour; neighbours differ by one shade.
Shade by face normal so faces jump when the light moves.
Use as few faces as still read: fewer faces, more character.
One card holds one object; icons and illustrations share the same faces.
Three shades per colour; dark faces lean warm purple.
motion: Triangles flip up from a flat sheet to assemble the object.
A slow light sweep makes faces jump shade in waves.
Objects reduce face count as they shrink into icons.

styles.name: ASCII Art
styles.idea: No pixels, only characters: brightness becomes glyph density, and noise resolves into the real label.
rules: Map luminance to character density along a ramp such as . , - ~ : ; = ! * # $ @.
Use a fixed monospaced cell of 0.6em by 1em.
Drive glyph and colour from the same light value.
Keep the cells fixed; animate by changing glyphs, not by moving cells.
Scrambled text always resolves into the actual final label.
motion: Decode: random glyphs settle left to right into the headline.
A rotating 3D form is rendered as characters.
Interface feedback is shown as glyphs flipping.

styles.name: Generative Art
styles.idea: Grow everything from one point with a seeded rule; change the seed, keep the family.
rules: A seed varies the image inside one visual family.
The same generator, version and parameters must reproduce the same frame.
Pick colours by weight, not uniformly.
Advance in small steps with an occupancy grid so ribbons never collide.
Place large forms first, then fill gaps with smaller ones.
motion: Ribbons grow from a single point outward on the beat.
The seed changes and the whole field regrows into a sibling pattern.
Each frame is a pure function of time so renders are repeatable.

styles.name: Point Cloud
styles.idea: Hundreds of thousands of points scan in, align and form surfaces: the look of a 3D capture.
rules: Points carry the form; there are no outlines or fills.
A single cyan accent marks scanning and measurement.
Density reveals importance: the subject is dense, context is sparse.
Show capture as a process: scan line, alignment, then surface.
Label measurements in mono with thin leader lines.
motion: A scan line sweeps and leaves points behind it.
Scattered points fly into lettering or an object.
The camera orbits slowly; points twinkle by depth.
avoid: claiming a real scan when it is a visual concept

styles.name: Liquid Chrome
styles.idea: A mirror surface that melts between letters and forms; the reflection is the colour.
rules: Chrome has no colour of its own; it shows a sky above and dark ground below, split by one bright horizon.
Shapes join and separate with smooth blends, like mercury.
Keep one tinted environment colour; the rest is neutral.
Edges stay crisp; highlights are sharp, not glowing.
Text on chrome needs a dark plate or very large size.
motion: Letters melt into a blob and re-form as the next word.
A slow turn makes the horizon highlight slide across the surface.
Drops merge and split on the beat.

styles.name: Ink Wash
styles.idea: Ink density is hierarchy, empty paper is composition, one vermilion seal says yes.
rules: Express hierarchy with ink density, from dense black to pale wash.
Brush width and dry strokes carry the energy; vary them within one stroke.
Leave at least a third of the frame empty.
Vermilion appears only as a seal or a confirm action.
Interface actions borrow ink: a drop, an expanding wash, a stamp.
motion: An ink drop lands and blooms outward as the transition.
Strokes are written in stroke order at brush speed.
The seal stamps last with a small press-and-lift.
avoid: running cursive faces whose characters read as other characters

styles.name: Plush
styles.idea: Soft silhouettes, dark roots and light tips, and fur that follows the body a moment late.
rules: Roots dark, tips light; vary length, direction and clumping.
Separate the silhouette from the ground with rim light.
Strands lag behind the body, overshoot and settle after it stops.
A press compresses and recovers like a cushion.
Keep shapes round and huggable; no sharp corners.
motion: A fur ball morphs into lettering, then objects.
Toggles slide and the fur catches up a beat later.
Like buttons squash and bounce back.
avoid: stiff fur that moves with the body

styles.name: Art Nouveau
styles.idea: No straight lines: a thick root bends gently, crosses one inflection, and curls ever tighter to a thin tip.
rules: No straight lines; curvature increases from root to tip.
Line width tapers about 10:1 from root to tip and ends in a point.
One gentle bend, one inflection, one tightening curl.
Frame text with growing vines rather than boxes.
Check curves by eye for steadily tightening curl toward the tip.
motion: Vines grow along their arc length, tips springing as they finish.
Frames are drawn as two mirrored whiplash curves.
Music in 3/4 suits the sway.
avoid: steps and sunbursts (that is Art Deco)

styles.name: Marker Illustration
styles.idea: Transparent marker strokes: overlaps get darker, paper white is reserved, a dab of white adds the highlight.
rules: One stroke is one layer; overlapping strokes darken the colour.
Reserve paper white before laying transparent colour.
Slower strokes leave darker ink pools at the ends.
Finish with a few opaque white highlights.
Lines are drawn, not traced: slight wobble, confident speed.
motion: Strokes draw on at hand speed, darker where they overlap.
Fills are laid as parallel strokes, not flood fills.
Highlights pop in last.

styles.name: New Wave Typography
styles.idea: Break the Swiss grid on purpose: overprint sheets, step letters, stretch tracking and shift blocks.
rules: Multiply colour sheets and keep each sheet's outline visible.
Step letters down by a quarter of their height to give reading a direction.
Let the same word travel from overlapping to very wide tracking.
Shift blocks and images but keep their edges on a 12-column grid.
Rotate the halftone grid 45 degrees and vary dot size for tone.
motion: A new colour sheet slides in and multiplies over the last.
The camera passes through the counter of an O.
Halftone dots grow to fill the screen, then snap into registration.
avoid: breaking the grid with no grid left

styles.name: Bento Grid
styles.idea: One idea per card; size is hierarchy; one gap, one radius.
rules: Each card holds one number, image or short message.
One hero card spans 2x2; supporting cards are 1x1, 2x1 or 1x2.
One gap value everywhere (20 px is a good start).
One corner system; nested radius = outer radius minus padding.
Rows and columns align; reflow cards for small screens instead of shrinking.
motion: Cards rise into their cells one by one, hero first.
The camera dives into one card, which becomes the next scene.
Numbers count up inside their cards on the beat.

styles.name: Masonry
styles.idea: Equal widths, natural heights, and each new card drops into the shortest column.
rules: Card widths are equal; heights follow the content.
Place each new card in the shortest column, ties left to right.
Horizontal and vertical gaps are equal.
Keep each image's original aspect ratio.
Reserve each card's height before its media loads.
motion: Cards fall into the shortest column in source order.
The whole wall scrolls slowly upward.
One card lifts out and expands to full frame.
